title: Sales enablement playbook — positioning, pricing, case studies, security FAQ
author: Ava Thompson
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook is a single-page reference for sales and pre-sales teams focused on prospect conversations for Redwood Inference. It consolidates positioning and messaging, competitive briefs, pitch-deck guidance, pricing guardrails, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this for enterprise and mid-market opportunities where proof of performance, cost predictability, and security posture drive buying decisions.

Key takeaways:
- Redwood competes on production-grade inference: predictable latency, cost controls, and deployment flexibility (hosted, dedicated, private).
- Focus dialogues on unit economics (tokens / second), SLOs, and integration effort.
- For security-sensitive prospects, lead with Private (VPC/on-prem) and our evidence (SOC2 + audit logging + KMS integrations).

1) Positioning & Messaging

Headline messaging (short): Redwood Inference — predictable, production-grade LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Core value props (talking points):
- Latency & reliability: GPU-optimized runtime with continuous batching and KV cache that reduces median token latency by up to 40% vs unmanaged endpoints.
- Cost & control: Intelligent batching, quantization profiles, and routing policies that reduce per-token cost while preserving quality.
- Deployment choices: Same API for hosted, reserved Dedicated capacity, and customer-managed Private installs (VPC / on-prem).
- Observability & ops: Per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, and rollout tools (canary/A-B/fallback).

Proof points & metrics to cite:
- Typical 95th percentile generation latency for 2k-context: 120–220ms on Dedicated (depending on model family).
- Unit cost reduction: 25–45% using recommended batching + KV caching for authenticated chat workloads.
- SLAs: 99.9% uptime on Dedicated contracts (see contract template).

Audience-specific hooks:
- Product/Engineering: Emphasize transparent performance benchmarks, SDK examples, and canary rollout controls.
- Platform/SRE: Emphasize capacity planning, autoscaling policies, and metrics/instrumentation exports.
- Security/Compliance: Emphasize Private deployment options, KMS/HSM support, and audit logging retention.

2) Competitive brief (short battlecards)

Competitors covered: Major managed LLM APIs, cloud-managed model endpoints, and inference vendors. Focus on three axes: latency/cost, deployment flexibility, and operational tooling.

Battlecard template (fast):
- Competitor: [Name]
- Typical strengths: [short bullets]
- Typical weaknesses vs Redwood: [short bullets]
- Effective rebuttals & demos: [short bullets]

Example: Cloud-Managed Endpoints (CME)
- Strengths: Seamless model hosting, large cloud integrations, fast time-to-first-call.
- Weaknesses vs Redwood: Higher per-token unit cost for high-throughput workloads; limited private/on-prem options and fewer per-route observability controls.
- Rebuttal: Demonstrate cost/run rate on a 500k-token/day benchmark and show Redwood Optimize recommendations that reduce bill by ~30% for real workloads.

Competitive differentiation matrix (talking bullets):
- If prospect cares most about latency predictability: push Redwood Dedicated.
- If prospect needs on-prem or VPC isolation for regulated data: push Redwood Private (include architecture references and SCIM/KMS notes).
- If prospect is evaluating pure price: show Optimize recommendations + quantization profiles and the projected TCO model.

3) Pitch deck structure & recommended slides

High-level deck outline (use for discovery -> technical deep dive):
1. Title + one-line problem statement (30s)
2. Vision & positioning (why Redwood)
3. Customer pain: latency/cost/unpredictability (data-backed)
4. Product overview: hosted, dedicated, private + console/observability
5. Architecture diagram: request flow, caching, routing, fallbacks
6. Performance benchmarks: latency & unit cost numbers (customer-specific if available)
7. Security & compliance: SOC2, audit logging, KMS/HSM, data residency options
8. Pricing & packaging: recommended tier for prospect (see pricing table)
9. Case study: 1–2 short wins with metrics
10. Implementation plan & timeline (pilot -> roll -> scale)
11. Next steps & ask (POC criteria, legal, POC/POC success metrics)

Sales talk tips per slide:
- Benchmarks: always pair with the prospect's expected concurrency/throughput and show a matched Redwood profile.
- Architecture slide: marker callouts for where data lives, encryption at rest/transit, and fallbacks.
- Pricing slide: show committed vs. variable scenarios and run simple monthly cost examples.

4) Pricing guidance (guardrails for AE/CS)

Pricing models we offer (short):
- Hosted (usage-based): per-token generation + embedding units; ideal for small to medium scale.
- Dedicated (committed): monthly reserved GPU capacity + overage pricing; ideal for predictable throughput.
- Private (enterprise): platform fee + deployment/maintenance; enterprise contract and support tiers.

Simple recommended tiers (example table):
Tier | Typical monthly commit | Included throughput | Ideal for
-----|-----------------------:|--------------------:|------------------
Starter | $2,000 | up to 100k tokens/day | Early integration / trials
Scale | $25,000 | up to 2M tokens/day | Product features in production
Enterprise | $150,000 | custom capacity & SLA | Platform teams, regulated data

Negotiation playbook (steps):
1. Confirm prospect's daily token volume & 95th percentile latency requirement.
2. Propose a pilot (2–6 weeks) with clear success metrics (e.g., latency < target, cost per session below X, throughput target).
3. Recommend a committed Dedicated quote when predictable 30-day run > 1.2M tokens/day or when SLO/uptime is required.
4. Offer optional add-ons: extended observability, longer data retention, premium SLAs.

Discounting & approval rules:
- Up to 20% discount: AE can approve for annual committed deals < $50k ARR.
- 20–40%: requires GTM director approval.
- >40%: requires VP-level approval and finance sign-off.

5) Representative case studies (short abstracts for pitch)

Case study A — Fintech Conversational Assistant (mid-market)\- Situation: Customer needed instant, secure responses for account inquiries with regulatory audit trails.\- Solution: Private deployment in customer VPC + Redwood Console for traceability; KV cache reduced duplicate computation.\- Outcomes: 42% reduction in per-query cost, median response latency 160ms, full auditability for compliance reviews.\- Contact / reference: internal customer reference (sales repo ID: FIN-2026-07).

Case study B — SaaS product search & summarization (AI-native startup)\- Situation: Heavy search traffic with spiky peaks; previously served by single-cloud endpoints causing cost spikes.\- Solution: Dedicated capacity + autoscaling burst policy; caching and batching recommended by Redwood Optimize.\- Outcomes: 35% lower monthly infrastructure cost, 3x higher throughput during bursts, reduced error rate by 70% after rollout.\- Contact / reference: internal customer reference (sales repo ID: SAAS-2026-11).

6) Security FAQ for prospects (explicit short answers for RFP/first-call)

Q: What certifications does Redwood hold?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II. For enterprise Private deployments we provide evidence packages as part of due diligence.

Q: How is customer data protected in hosted deployments?
A: Data in transit is TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption via cloud provider KMS. Customer tokens are logically separated per-tenant and logs are stored with RBAC access.

Q: What key-management options are available?
A: Hosted: we use cloud KMS with per-tenant key scoping. Dedicated & Private: we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault).

Q: Can we run Redwood on-prem / air-gapped?
A: Yes — our Private offering supports on-prem packaging and an air-gapped install with an optional offline license and manual upgrade procedures. See the onprem-packaging reference.

Q: How long are audit logs retained and can retention be customized?
A: Default retention is 90 days for hosted; retention customizations available as an add-on for Dedicated and Private. Audit logs can be exported to customer SIEM.

Q: Does Redwood perform model content filtering or data minimization?
A: We provide configurable data retention policies and optional PII redaction at the ingestion layer. We also support in-flight request filtering rules in the console for sensitive endpoints.

8) Implementation plan template (pilot -> production)

Pilot (2–6 weeks):
1. Kickoff & discovery (3–5 days) — confirm success criteria and datasets.
2. Provision environment — hosted sandbox or Dedicated trial capacity.
3. Ingest sample traffic and run Redwood Optimize recommendations (batching/quantization).
4. Measure success (latency, cost, quality), complete security questionnaire.
5. Decision: scale to Dedicated or scope Private deployment.

Production roll (8–12 weeks typical):
- Week 0–2: Contracting & security onboarding
- Week 2–6: Dedicated capacity provisioning / Private deployment prep
- Week 6–10: Integration, telemetry, and canary rollout
- Week 10–12: Full cutover and post-launch 30-day hypercare

9) Playbook checklist (for AE / Solutions Engineer before POC)
- [ ] Confirm expected 95th percentile latency & target concurrency
- [ ] Determine whether data residency / VPC / on-prem is required
- [ ] Gather sample traffic/profile and expected monthly tokens
- [ ] Prepare a benchmark slide matched to prospect's profile
- [ ] Identify legal & security contacts and start NDA/RFI flow if needed
